chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamilah, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far, who said: My brother narrated to me, from Ja'far, from his father.

He went to Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) with a drink on the night in which he passed away, and he said: O my father, drink this. He said: O my son, this is the night in which I shall be taken, and it is the night in which Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was taken.

key_terms.أَبِيهِ: his father; referring to the preceding paternal transmitter in the sanad
key_terms.بِشَرَابٍ: with a drink; what was brought to the Imam
key_terms.جَعْفَرٍ: Ja'far; the Imam named in the chain of transmission
key_terms.حَدَّثَنِي: narrated to me; an isnad transmission expression
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah; the Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.عَلِيَّ بْنَ الْحُسَيْنِ: Ali ibn al-Husayn; the Imam spoken of in the report
key_terms.قُبِضَ: was taken; a reverential expression for death or passing away
key_terms.لَيْلَةً: a night; the specific night of passing referred to in the narration

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show that Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) knew the night of his passing?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) knew the time of his passing and explicitly identified the night of his death. It reflects the doctrine that the Imams (عليهم السلام) possess divinely granted knowledge concerning their death, and it also preserves a moment of intimate exchange between father and son.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Abdullah Bin Abu Ja’far who said, 
‘My brother narrated to me, from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>,

that he<sup>asws</sup> went over to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> with a drink on the night in which he<sup>asws</sup> passed away, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O father<sup>asws</sup>! Drink this’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>! This is the night in which I<sup>asws</sup> shall pass away, and it is the night in which Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> passed away’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from abu Jamilah from ‘Abdallah ibn abu Ja‘far who has said that my brother narrated from Ja‘far (abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) from his father

that he went to Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) on the night in which he passed away and offered him a drink requesting, “Father, please drink it.” He said, “Son, this is the night in which I will pass away and during such night the Messenger of Allah also passed away.” (The date of the demise of the two holy ones, as generally held, is not the same. However, being the same day is a possibility).
